nmpilot

nmpilot is an R package that drives a population pharmacokinetic (popPK) analysis with NONMEM from R, from the data set to the final model diagnostics. It calls the NONMEM nmfe launcher directly and does not need PsN or Wings for NONMEM. Wings is optional: runs can sit next to their control streams or in run subdirectories, and the Wings conventions (.reg run directories, .smr files, extended control streams with parameter labels) are also read, so that projects started with Wings can be continued.

Status: version 0.9.0, under active development. The interface may still change. Bug reports and suggestions are welcome in the issues.

New name: the package was called nmtools up to version 0.7.1. It was renamed nmpilot to avoid confusion with an unrelated GitHub repository of the same name in the same field. If you installed nmtools, remove it with remove.packages("nmtools"), install nmpilot as below, and replace library(nmtools) by library(nmpilot) in your scripts.

Installation

The simplest way is R-universe, which provides ready-built binaries for Windows and macOS (no compilation, no remotes package needed):

install.packages("nmpilot",
                 repos = c("https://nskoch.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

The development version can also be installed from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("nskoch/nmpilot")

# with the vignettes:
remotes::install_github("nskoch/nmpilot", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Running models requires a working NONMEM installation. The package is developed and used on Windows with NONMEM 7.4 and 7.6 (nmfe74.bat, nmfe76.bat). On Linux and macOS, give the path of the nmfe script (for example /opt/nm760/run/nmfe76, which must be executable): every function that runs NONMEM calls it directly. This was checked on Linux with a simulated nmfe, not yet with a real NONMEM installation. Reading outputs, diagnostics and plots work without NONMEM, on outputs of NONMEM 7.1 to 7.6.

What the package covers

Step Functions
Read and explore the data set nm_read_csv(), nm_data_previsual(), nm_plot_dv(), nm_summary(), nm_add_rate(), nm_export_data()
Suggest a structural model before any run nm_suggest_model() (compartments, input, elimination, error model, initial values, hard-to-estimate parameters, alerts), nm_suggest_design() (expected RSE and shrinkage), nm_suggest_run() (run and rank the candidates), nm_suggest_covariates() (covariate screening on individual estimates)
Write a control stream nm_write_ctl() (compartmental PK model), nm_ctl_mu() (MU referencing), nm_ctl_iov() (inter-occasion variability), nm_ctl_m3() (M3 method for BQL data), nm_ctl_check() (static check)
Run NONMEM nm_run() (n_cores: several runs at the same time), nm_cores(), nm_convert_ctl() (Wings extended control stream to standard NONMEM)
Read the results of one or several runs nm_extract_runs() (also several $EST or $PROB, IOV, $MIX, failed or interrupted runs), nm_filter_runs(), nm_compare_runs(), nm_extract_run_table() (Word table)
Identify what each THETA / ETA means nm_identify_parameters(), nm_identify_directory()
Goodness-of-fit diagnostics nm_gof()
Compare two runs nm_compare() (paired CWRES / NPDE, individual OFV; Vuong and Clarke tests for non-nested models, bootstrap, gain map, overlaid diagnostics)
Improve a base model from one evaluation run nm_optimize_base() (residual error, random effects and covariates ranked on a linearised model), nm_derivatives_ctl()
VPC and pc-VPC nm_vpc_ctl(), nm_vpc()
Parameter uncertainty nm_profile() (likelihood profile), nm_bootstrap() (case bootstrap); both accept n_cores
Influential subjects nm_jackknife() (leave-one-subject-out jackknife: OFV change and THETA shifts)
Covariate assessment on the ETA distributions nm_wasserstein() (Wasserstein distance, Simon et al. 2026)
Export figures nm_export_plot()

Example project and vignettes

The package ships a small example project, with simulated data (60 fictitious subjects, one-compartment oral model) and the NONMEM outputs of a BASE and a FINAL model, so that every function that reads results can be tried without NONMEM:

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "nmpilot")
runs <- nm_extract_runs(ex)

Two vignettes use it: vignette("nmpilot") (getting started, from the data set to the comparison of two models) and vignette("wasserstein").

A typical workflow 

library(nmpilot)

# 1. Data set: read, summarise, plot
dat <- nm_read_csv("C:/nm76g64/run/study/data.csv")
nm_summary(dat$data)
nm_plot_dv(dat$data, scales = "both")

# 2. Suggest a structural model and write its control stream
s <- nm_suggest_model("C:/nm76g64/run/study/data.csv", dose_conc_factor = 1000)
s                                   # ranked candidates, initial values, alerts
nm_write_ctl("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run1.ctl", from = s, candidate = 1)
#    or write a control stream from the columns of the data set
nm_write_ctl("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.ctl",
             input = "C:/nm76g64/run/study/data.csv", error = "combined")

# 3. Run one or several models. By default each run goes to <run>.reg/ in the
#    analysis directory; run_subdir = "" runs it next to its control stream.
#    A relative $DATA path is read from the control stream folder
#    ($DATA data.csv) or from the run directory ($DATA ../data.csv).
log <- nm_run(
  ctl          = c("run1.ctl", "run2.ctl"),
  nmfe_path    = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
  analysis_dir = "C:/nm76g64/run/study"
)

# 4. Results of all the runs of the project
runs <- nm_extract_runs("C:/nm76g64/run/study")
runs                          # OFV, dOFV, minimisation and covariance status
nm_compare_runs(runs)         # parameters side by side
nm_extract_run_table("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg")   # Word table

# 5. Diagnostics, and comparison of two models
gof <- nm_gof("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg/sdtab2")
plot(gof)
cmp <- nm_compare("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run1.reg",
                  "C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg",
                  labels = c("Base", "+ WT on CL"))
plot(cmp)

# 6. VPC / pc-VPC
nm_vpc_ctl("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.ctl",
           nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat", n_sim = 500)
nm_vpc("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.ctl",
       col_names = c("NSIM", "ID", "TIME", "AMT", "MDV", "DV", "PRED", "IPRED"),
       type = 2)

# 7. Uncertainty
prof <- nm_profile("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg/run2.ctl",
                   "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
                   param = "CL", from = 2, to = 6, by = 0.25)
plot(prof, type = "dofv")
boot <- nm_bootstrap("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg/run2.ctl",
                     nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
                     n = 500, seed = 1)

Run layouts (Wings not required)

nm_run() writes each run either in its own subdirectory or directly in the folder of its control stream:

run_subdir Outputs of run1.ctl
".reg" (default) run1.reg/run1.lst, run1.reg/run1.ext… (same layout as Wings)
".run" or any suffix run1.run/run1.lst…
"" run1.lst, run1.ext… next to run1.ctl (as a manual nmfe call)

nm_extract_run_table(), nm_vpc_ctl() and nm_vpc() find a run in <run>.reg/, <run>.nm7/, a folder named <run>, or directly in the analysis directory. nm_extract_runs() reads every run of a folder, in subdirectories or not. nm_wasserstein() and nm_compare() take a run directory of any name or a run prefix ("C:/study/run1" for C:/study/run1.ext, run1.phi…), and nm_gof() a table file or the folder that holds it. Control streams in Wings label syntax are converted automatically by nm_run() (this needs a run subdirectory) or by nm_convert_ctl().

Several NONMEM runs at the same time

nm_run(), nm_profile(), nm_jackknife(), nm_bootstrap(), nm_vpc_ctl() and nm_suggest_run() take an n_cores argument (default 1: one run after the other). Each run is then started in the background from its own folder, at most n_cores at a time. n_cores = "auto" uses the physical cores minus one; n_cores = "ask" shows the cores and asks the number once per R session.

nm_cores()          # logical and physical cores
log <- nm_run(sprintf("run%d.ctl", 1:4), "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
              "C:/nm76g64/run/study", n_cores = 4)
jk  <- nm_jackknife("C:/nm76g64/run/study/run2.reg/run2.ctl",
                    nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat", n_cores = "auto")

Writing control streams

nm_write_ctl() writes a complete control stream for a 1- to 3-compartment PK model: IV or extravascular administration; first-order, zero-order (modelled rate R1 = K0 with RATE = -1, or modelled duration D1 with RATE = -2) or transit-compartment absorption; linear or Michaelis-Menten elimination; analytic (ADVAN/TRANS) or ODE solution. $INPUT follows the column order of the data set. Three functions then transform a control stream, generated or written by hand, and nm_ctl_check() looks for THETA/ETA/EPS used without a declaration and other static inconsistencies.

ctl <- nm_write_ctl(input = c("ID", "TIME", "DV", "AMT", "EVID", "MDV", "CMT", "OCC", "BQL"),
                    cpts = 2, error = "combined",
                    theta_init = c(CL = 3, V2 = 30), iiv = c(CL = 30, V2 = 25, KA = 50))
ctl <- nm_ctl_iov(ctl, parameters = "CL", n_occ = 2)   # $ABBR REPLACE + BLOCK SAME
ctl <- nm_ctl_m3(ctl, lloq = 0.1)                       # M3 likelihood, LAPLACE
nm_ctl_check(ctl)
nm_ctl_mu(nm_write_ctl())                               # MU referencing for SAEM/IMP

The same functions are available as a Shiny application: https://nicolas-simon.shinyapps.io/nonmem_ctl_publi/.

Suggesting a structural model

nm_suggest_model() looks at the data before any NONMEM run: NCA and sums of exponentials on each rich dosing interval (or on naive pooled data when the sampling is sparse) give the support for 1, 2 or 3 compartments, for the input model (first-order, lag time, zero-order, transit), for linear or saturable elimination and for an additive, proportional or combined error. Candidates come with initial values in the names used by nm_write_ctl(), the parameters likely to be hard to estimate, and, for linear models, the expected RSE and eta-shrinkage for the sampling design.

s <- nm_suggest_model("data.csv", dose_conc_factor = 1000)   # mg and ng/mL
s$candidates
plot(s, "profiles")
nm_suggest_design(s, candidate = 1, times = c(1, 4, 12))     # another design
nm_suggest_covariates(s, covariates = c("WT", "SEX"))
r <- nm_suggest_run(s, analysis_dir = "C:/nm76g64/run/study",
                    nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat", candidates = 1:3)

The scores rank candidates; they are no substitute for model comparison in NONMEM. The validation script inst/validation/validate_suggest_model.R measures how often the true structure is recovered on simulated datasets.

Parameter names from the model code

nm_identify_parameters() reads $PK (or $PRED) and links every THETA and ETA to the PK parameter it acts on, with a role: typical value, covariate effect (power, exponential, linear, saturable or conditional), IIV scale or residual error. nm_extract_runs() uses it so that results are labelled CL, V, KA… rather than THETA1, THETA2. Wings control streams that use labels (CL = POPCL*EXP(eta_cl)) are handled.

x <- nm_identify_parameters("run2.ctl")
x$parameter_table

Wasserstein-based covariate assessment

nm_wasserstein() implements the method of Simon N, Hulot JS, von Fabeck K. Distribution-based covariate assessment using Wasserstein distance in population pharmacokinetic models. Front Pharmacol. 2026;17:1804989 (doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1804989). It compares the distribution of an ETA between groups of subjects defined by a covariate, for one or several runs, and reports a Wasserstein-based R2.

w <- nm_wasserstein(c(BASE = "base.reg", FINAL = "final.reg"),
                    covariates = c("CLCR", "CT01"), eta = "CL")
w
plot(w)
plot(w, type = "r2w")

Citation 

citation("nmpilot")

gives the reference of the package and, for nm_jackknife() and nm_wasserstein(), the reference of the original method. Each release is archived on Zenodo with its own DOI; the DOI badge above (10.5281/zenodo.24244339) cites all versions and resolves to the latest one. The archives up to v0.7.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24406632) carry the former name, nmtools. The releases v0.6.0 and v0.7.0 were made by mistake on the commit of version 0.5.0 and hold its code: use v0.7.1 or later.
